# tom: the metrics HE chose

From sweep 3 (see `../METRICS-THEY-CHOSE.md`). Kept here verbatim so the
corpus carries his units, not the schema's.

- **12 of 14**: the fourteen stairs at home, climbed without stopping,
  against the flight he built the bannister for twenty years ago. This is
  the CANONICAL sweep-3 stairs fraction (see
  `../METRICS-THEY-CHOSE.md`) - his, verbatim. Rachel independently counts
  her own fourteen stairs in her own house; the convergence is deliberate
  and both this file and hers say so. The divergence is the more
  interesting half: rachel's fraction is at least logged, in degraded form,
  as a `checks.jsonl` pass/fail row with the true fraction surviving in the
  note. His is never logged anywhere machine-readable. It lives only here.
  Two of eight athletes independently invented a fraction-shaped stairs
  metric; only one of the two ever touches the schema. Both are G79
  evidence (see FINDINGS.md, `tom-E8`).
- **Belt holes**, against the belt he wore at his wedding in 2009, kept in a
  drawer since. "That's my actual scale, more than any number on the
  bathroom one." The corpus encodes the closest available proxy - the
  waist-tape measurements - because a belt-hole count itself has no schema
  home either; the tape is the nearest honest stand-in, not the same thing.
- **Fares in a row before needing a ten-minute sit.** Occupational capacity,
  unschema'd, G79. Never appears in any dataset.
- **Finished a job at work without needing a breather he didn't used to
  need.** Same category as the fares count; occupational, private, never
  logged.
- **Times he got outside with Jack, even just to the postbox and back.**
  Relational, counted privately, not in the record.
- **Did he read to Jack, even for two minutes.** Same as above.
- **Good day / bad day "in myself"**: some days he feels like a man of 53,
  some days like an old fella, and it is not always the same day as the good
  numbers. Affective, private, never logged.
- **Evenings he wasn't the last one still at the table, picking at
  nothing.** Affective, private.
- **Nights in a row without the vending machine at the rank** - distinct
  from priya's 3am hospital-machine streak, same shape of metric, different
  life. This is the one item from this list that DOES leave a trace in the
  record: the journal claim dated 2029-12-20 (LIES.md T2). The streak count
  itself is never logged; only the claim about it is, once, and nothing
  else in the record can confirm or contradict it.
- **Times he said yes instead of "you go on, I'll wait here."** Affective,
  private.

## What he explicitly does not have

An app. Any of it. The record's raggedness - the batch transcription, the
"nearly absent" daily file, the total absence of steps or sleep or heart
rate anywhere - is not a data gap to be filled. It is the shape of a life
that keeps its numbers on paper and its real metrics in his head.
